key_insight: Global relaxed entropy-energy states can be constructed for dynamic thermoplasticity even when the temperature-dependent yield set collapses, but macroscopic Prandtl-Reuss normality is not guaranteed.
engineering_relevance: The analysis clarifies constitutive limits for thermomechanical models whose plastic strength can vanish at finite temperature, without viscosity or hardening regularization.
method: One-parameter Temam-Norton-Hoff-Galerkin approximation with an undiscretized heat equation.
Entropy-weighted estimates establish logarithmic-temperature compactness and stress admissibility.
Measure-valued limits and compact-fibre lifts encode exact normality and maximum plastic work.
evidence_signal: Analytical results include an O(sqrt(log n/n)) overstress convergence rate in every fixed finite Lebesgue space and an explicit smooth counterexample to macroscopic normality; the abstract reports no numerical validation.
watch_item: Available compactness does not identify a canonical macroscopic stress-plastic-flow pairing, and fully collapsed regimes may lose finite-measure plastic flow or the full displacement boundary trace.
paper_title: Dynamic Prandtl-Reuss Thermoplasticity with Degenerating Yield Constraints
